sections.what_happened: Media projections now give Democrats at least 53 Senate seats (Nikkei: AP had called 51 overnight; later projections add seats) and 221 House seats with 85 races still uncalled (AP via Nikkei). Michigan: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in the Senate race; in his victory speech he said 'It shouldn't be this hard to pay your taxes and know that that money is going to be spent on you and your kids instead of dropping bombs on somebody else and their kids.' El-Sayed is an Egyptian-American doctor and a staunch critic of the US war on Iran. This updates 1100-01 (AP calls House; Democrats control both chambers) with a firmer Senate number and the Michigan result, which the pre-1100 reporting had left as a competitive seat Democrats might not hold.
sections.what_verified: 1 declared family: Nikkei Asia (T2). AP figures arrive via Nikkei relay; AP has no separate declared tier entry in the registry excerpt checked. El-Sayed speech via AJ liveblog (T2, STATE QA) is a second claim, not corroboration of the seat count.
sections.what_disputed: 85 House races still uncalled, so the House margin is not final; Senate seats in still-uncalled competitive races could move the total. Trump's VETO posture (recorded 0900-01) is the standing counterweight to any Democratic legislative agenda, including on the Iran war.
sections.why_matters: Midterm follow-up Short: the war critic who just won a Senate seat says your taxes should not fund bombs on other people's kids -- while Trump holds the veto. The 53-seat number is the hard count in the title.
